correctness.rationale: In odd degree the invariant top apolar pairing is alternating and perfect. The nonzero quadratic moment map spans the unique quadratic-output representation of dimension three, so dμ has rank dim(sl2·f), and the radial direction is in its kernel on μ=0. By the three-quadric complete intersection, projective rank loss is the singular locus. Nonzero semisimple operators have only nonzero odd weights, and nonzero nilpotents have one-dimensional kernels consisting of pure powers after conjugation; the pure powers lie on the zero fiber. Near x^r the change x→x+uy keeps a0=1 and translates a1, giving a product with the slice a1=0. Differentiating the binomial-normalized form r-1 times gives the displayed quadrics. The pivots a_(r-1),a_r are linear with coefficient 2 on this slice, solvable successively; substitution preserves weights, and the remaining equation has weight r+1. Its quadratic terms pair each index i=3,…,r-2 with r+1-i, with nonzero coefficients of the same sign on both sides of each pair; a2 is its only quadratic kernel direction. The analytic implicit-function theorem produces a unique critical section in the paired variables; the analytic splitting lemma leaves its critical value. Weight covariance with wt(a2)=2 forces the critical value to be c·a2^((r+1)/2). If c were zero, the split slice would contain a singular curve, contrary to the global rank calculation and the fact that only x^r lies in the pure-power orbit on the slice. Over C rescale c to one. Since (r+1)/2=p+2, the Fitting ideal of the resulting hypersurface times smooth curve gives completed ring C[[u,t]]/(t^(p+1)); its generic length times deg(C_r)=r yields the asserted cycle degree. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; its low-degree computations are not needed for the universal proof.
